language_semantics.arithmetic: unbounded mathematical integers (Python int); no overflow or division
language_semantics.grammar: assignments and print statements; integer literals/variables; +, -, *, unary -, and parentheses
language_semantics.side_effects: expressions are pure; print output is the only observable program result
language_semantics.undefined_variables: rejected during lowering and AST evaluation

limitations: The language is intentionally tiny and has no input, control flow, functions, memory, or division.
Only print output is observable; removing assignments that cannot reach print is therefore semantics-preserving.
Pass ordering is trained on one separate synthetic program and may not generalize to other workloads.
The generated bytecode is executed by a Python educational VM, so wall time mostly reflects interpreter overhead.
Short compile and execution measurements vary with host load; all raw repeats are retained.

pass_order_optimization.constraints: apply each of four passes exactly once
pass_order_optimization.objective: lexicographically minimize final instruction count, then encoded code bytes
